title.narrative: BF SAT Malawi

description.narrative: Millions of young people do not have access to appropriate, gender-responsive, quality SRHR education, information and services. This makes them vulnerable to unintended pregnancies, often followed by child marriage (CM). The Break Free! programme empowers adolescents and young people to make their own free and informed choices to speak out and have control over their SRH and lives. BF! is tackling root causes of gender inequality, unequal power relations and discriminatory social norms, systems, structures, policies and practices, supported by civil society and improved legislation. The project will be implemented between 2021 and 2025 by the Break Free! Consortium consisting of Plan International Netherlands, SAT and FAWE, technical partners KIT and RMT in collaboration with Dutch Embassies. It will be carried out in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Sudan and Zambia, in addition to a regional Pan-African component to sustain the country programmes.

The primary target group of the Break Free programme consists if girls and young women (GYW) aged 10 -24. To effectuate change in the lives of those GYW, the programme engages other stakeholders such as government, CSOs, parents and/or caretakers and the community at large in the 9 focus countries of Break Free!

The strategic programme objective of: adolescents exercise their right to live free from TP and CM, supported by civil society is contributing the above-defined impact. To achieve this strategic objective, CSOs, youth-led groups and networks will be strengthened to lobby and advocate for improved legislation and implementation to increase girls’ agency and to promote social norm change in favour of the prevention of CM/TP, and in some countries FGM/C. Although norm change takes time and the strategic objective is formulated under the ‘sphere of influence’ over which we do not have full control, the programme will report reduced prevalence of CM and TP for groups of girls in the programme locations, by 2025. The following three pathways of change lead towards the strategic programme objective.Outcome 1: Adolescent girls at risk of CM/TP access quality and safe education,Outcome 2: Duty bearers and decision-makers develop, resource and implement laws and policies that respond to adolescents’ needs, andOutcome 3: Adolescents access quality SRHR information, education and services.

title.narrative: Number of adolescents aged 10-24 reached with SRHR information/education
# of young people (female) reached with comprehensive, correct information on sexuality, HIV/AIDS, STIs, pregnancy and contraception

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of female youths (aged 10 - 24 years) that are reached by CSE though the activities implemented by the program. The indicator counts in school and out of school youths.

comment.narrative: The programme will provide comprehensive, correct information on sexuality, HIV/AIDS, STIs, pregnancy and contraception to youth groups, hubs and clubs that cover in-school and out-of-school youths. BF! Will provide mentorship sessions, life skills training, SRHR information and stipulation of MYP. CSE provision and integrated SRHR services will be supported with YouthWyze outreaches and in-reaches to create a conducive environment through enforcement of community by-laws by traditional leaders. The programme will also incorporate the use of various media to bring about positive behaviour change and address negative attitudes on SRHR and harmful cultural practices including CM/TP.

A total of 41000 adolescents were reached with SRHR information and Education. This data was from Machinga and Lilongwe District Health Offices. In addition, 3.017 were reached through YouthWyze, 17.216 through Timasuke pa Zaumoyo Wathu radio programme.

The data collected with the District Health Offices in Machinga and Lilongwe, reveals that the target for 2024 has been exceeded. Key contributors to this success include youth-led awareness initiatives, YouthWyze outreaches, SRHR sessions through Champions of Change and Theatre for Development, as well as the Timasuke Pa Zaumoyo Wathu radio program. The program leveraged these platforms to enhance its reach to inform and educate young people in age-appropriate sexual reproductive health and rights.

The participants reached are aged 10-24. Activities entail provision of SRHR information, education, counselling and services through YouthWyze Outreaches, Timasuke pa za Umoyo Wathu Radio Program slots and community intergenerational dialogues.

The program leveraged these platforms to enhance its reach to inform and educate young people in age-appropriate sexual reproductive health and rights.

The internet, radio, SMS and physical meetings were used to disseminate SRHR information to youth, educating and Chiwalo. The Clubs provided safe spaces for discussion on critical matters of SRHR, gender equality and social norms. BF!’s weekly radio program on Timveni radio called “Timasuke pa zaumoyo wathu” reached 47,394 (28,436 female, 18,958 males) listeners and 1, 200 were also reached through SMS. The broadcast informed youths on SRHR matters and offered an opportunity for youth to ask and receive expert advice on matters which are not readily discussed in their communities. A Facebook page ofYouthWyze games was also used to disseminate SRHR information. The YouthWyze Games were adapted and extended to youths without internet access using outreach and in-reach activities in hard to reach areas. The initiative proved to be effective as 8,234 (4,742 females and 3,492 males) were reached out with comprehensive Sexual Reproductive-Youth Friendly Health Services education, information, and serviceshence increased knowledge on SRHR. on HIV and AIDS, contraceptives, relationships and gender equality. Twenty-two champions of change clubs were formed in Njewa.

description.narrative: This indicator serves to establish the reach of the programme by counting the number of civil society organisations (CSOs) that are not youth or women led and are 2nd tier partners in the programme, i.e., CSO partners directly contracted by any of the 1st tier partners within the scope of the implementation of the Break Free! programme.

comment.narrative: These are strategically selected youth-led CSOs and CSOs which are not women led/youth led but working in girls’ education and health and implementing programmes that are similar or complimentary to the BF! Programme at national, district and community level. The CSOs’ will add value to the programme by providing supporting lobby and advocacy voices and fostering dialogues between adolescents, young people and duty bearers, and advocating for implementation of laws and policies that respond to the needs of young people.

Break Free! works with Youth Response for Social Change, Global Hope Mobilization and Timveni as 2nd tier partners. GLOHOMO and Youth Response for Social Change are contracted by SAT to carryout outreaches in the impact areas. Timveni Child and Youth radio station contracted by PLAN to broadcast a radio program called "Timasukilane pa za umoyo".

PLAN, FAWEMA and SAT collaborated to achieve set targets for 2022 working with targeted youth- and non-youth led CSOs. The consortium achieved its targets but under increased difficulty at national level as Human Rights Defenders were facing difficulty in holding government accountable and accessing fundamental freedoms amidst worsening human rights conditions.There were violations of rights, harassment of civil society actors and enactment of repressive laws with unclear, overbearing, overstepping or outright brutal enforcement parameters by government agencies. This hostile environment led to the actors in Malawi making efforts to engage government to create a conducive/enabling operational environment for CSO activities.It was noted through these engagements that government was showing willingness to engage and work with CSOs.
BF! will continue working with Youth Response for Social Change and Timven Radio.

title.narrative: # of youth led CSOs included in SPs programmes

description.narrative: This indicator serves to establish the reach of the programme by counting the number of youth led civil society organisations (CSOs) that are 2nd tier partners in the programme, i.e., CSO partners directly contracted by any of the 1st tier partners within the scope of the implementation of the Break Free! programme.

comment.narrative: PLAN, FAWEMA and SAT collaborated to achieve set targets for 2022 working with targeted youth- and non-youth led CSOs. The consortium achieved its targets but under increased difficulty at national level as Human Rights Defenders were facing difficulty in holding government accountable and accessing fundamental freedoms amidst worsening human rights conditions. There were violations of rights, harassment of civil society actors and enactment of repressive laws with unclear, overbearing, overstepping or outright brutal enforcement parameters by government agencies. This hostile environment led to the actors in Malawi making efforts to engage government to create a conducive/enabling operational environment for CSO activities. It was noted through these engagements that government was showing willingness to engage and work with CSOs.
The programme will drop one partner (GLOHOMO) and remain with the Youth Response for social change (YRSC) and Timveni Radio station.

The program continued with contracts for two youth focused community-based organizations (CBOs): Youth Response for Social Change (YRSC) and Timveni Child and Youth Media Organization (TCYMO). TCYMO is a media organization based in Malawi that operates on both radio and television platforms. The BF! contract gave youth a platform to advocate for their rights and engage with national issues in TCYMO’s radio broadcasts, covering topics such as news, culture, sports, and youth empowerment. Youth Response is a grassroots organization dedicated to empowering young people, particularly adolescent girls and young women. The partnership with BF! addressed gender-based violence, promoted education, and advocacy for SRHR. Additionally, YRSC engaged in governance, human rights, and sustainable development efforts.

These are strategically selected youth-led CSOs and CSOs which are not women led/youth led but working in girls’ education and health and implementing programmes that are similar or complimentary to the BF! Programme at national, district and community level. The CSOs’ will add value to the programme by providing supporting lobby and advocacy voices and fostering dialogues between adolescents, young people and duty bearers, and advocating for implementation of laws and policies that respond to the needs of young people.

title.narrative: Number of CSOs (not youth led) who report having strengthened lobby & advocacy capacities
# of CSOs (not youth or women led) with increased L&A capacities

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of CSOs that are not led by youth or women and record increased lobby and advocacy capacity. Break Free! programme has developed a standard capacity assessment tool to measure the change in targeted CSOs.

comment.narrative: The programme will strengthen Lobby and advocacy capacity of targeted CSOs including, participation in the review of laws and policies scorecard, budget tracking, lobbying for increased funding, specific needs: budget tracking, lobbying for increased funding, participation.

Community level engagements, and exchange rate, favoured more local engagements than initially planned. The program supported trainings and capacity in action mentoring Achieved improvements in organizational strengths have included the establishment of a clear mission, vision, theories of change, and strategic plans for advocating SRHR. The CSOs have reported that their leaders are now more proactive and pragmatic in addressing external opportunities and risks. CSOs have become skilled at collaborating within networks, effectively identifying potential entry points for engagement, and gaining recognition from communities and policymakers as credible advocates for the issues they address. They have developed a deeper and broader understanding of their core constituency - girls and women - along with strategies for engaging with them in meaningful and effective ways.

Malawi: The BF! Used a CSO self-administered capacity assessment tool to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of CSO structures and functions. Capacity building trainning and gudiance were undertaken to improve CSO’s conduct of advocacy initiatives with duty bearers at community, district and national level around SRHR, education, adopting positive social norms and meaningful youth participation, and leadership. BF! also collaborated with the African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC) to expose its partner CSOs to capacity strengthening in value clarification, attitudes transformation and sexuality education. Improved performance was seen in partners as they jointly advocated for the revision of Community Victim Support Unit (CVSU) guidelines, increased health budget allocation, addressed stock-out challenges through engagements with relevant stakeholders, interface engagement on scorecard findings. Specific CSOs were targeted with training on the National Girls Education Network in advocacy as well as oriented on the Presidentof Zambia’s UNGA commitments to transform education. BF! led CSO trainings also resulted in preparing action plans for joint advocacy initiatives related to girls' education and SRHR issues.

The programme is targeting select CSOs in Njewa and Chiwalo to improve their capacity for lobby and advocacy, participation in networks and consortium, interaction with policy makers and duty bearers on gender equality and SRHR and how to promote accountability in the delivery of SRHR services through social accountability mechanisms. None-youth led CSOs will be trained on how to lobby for increased funding, budget management and how to monitor governments using scorecards and track government expenditure.

The results with youth-led CSOs was achieved by targeting women and men-lead organizations as 3rd tier which include Women Forum, Malawi Girls Guide Association (MAGGA), Oxfam, Youth Impact, and Save the Children. Members of CSEC which included Rays of Hope, Oxfam, Font of Nations, and Active Youth Initiative for Social Enhancement (AYISE). The capacity was in form of budget analysis, through presentation of education budget analysis. The results with non-youth-led was achieved by targeting youth structures in the two impact areas. BF is continuously mentoring and building the capacity of youth groups in the impact areas.
Capacity strengthening on lobby and advocacy, participation, review of laws and policies scorecard, budget tracking, lobbying for increased funding, and other organization specific needs.
